newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl sees '97 growth 2.5-2.7 pct, '98 3 pct -TV.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sees '97 growth 2.5-2.7 pct, '98 3 pct -TV.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday he expects German economic output to grow 2.5 to 2.7 percent this year, accelerating to three percent next year, according to a transcript of a television interview.

"We will surely have growth of 2.5, 2.6, 2.7 percent in gross national product this year. I am sure that next year we will reach three percent. That is a good goal, but we will only reach it if we support it with tax changes," Kohl said.
"The goal is to reduce unemployment, to create new jobs, and the economy, which thank God is coming along," Kohl said in the interview with RTL television.
Kohl said he holds fast to the goal of halving unemployment by the year 2000, although he recognises that the chance of reaching it is much lower than before.
"If we don't reach the goal right away, and if we reach only a third instead of half, we will still have achieved something," he said.
